title: The Missing Portrait
premise: Petra Whitlock, a concierge whose gift for noticing has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral of hotel owner Marguerite Vale — a letter that names him as its intended confessor and insists the death was murder. As he investigates, he discovers the killer is someone inside the hotel's found family of staff, someone who has memorized both the case file and Petra's own methods, staging the crime to frame an innocent porter. To stop a second killing planned for the anniversary dinner, Petra must lay a trap using the one detail the killer couldn't have known from any file; the trap works, but exposing the truth means choosing between legal justice and mercy for a survivor of the Vales' old cruelties.
about_author: Noor Quintana spent a decade working night desks in grand hotels across three continents, collecting the small human dramas that unfold after midnight. She writes mysteries about people who are invisible to power but see everything.

chapters.title: The Day After
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Three days after Marguerite Vale's funeral, a letter arrives at the Hotel Aurelian confessing to her murder and naming Petra as its recipient. The postmark is dated the day after she died. Petra rereads it obsessively, recognizing a staged detail — the writer describes a room he could never have entered. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of being seen at last.

chapters.title: What the Concierge Knows
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He reviews his private notes on three past 'accidents' he solved silently, establishing his method: keys, timings, small kindnesses remembered. He begins mapping who had access to Marguerite's suite, suspecting the police file itself was used to design the crime. Emotional beat: quiet competence shadowed by loneliness — no one knows what he carries.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Detective Ilsa Reyes, who resents reopening the case but can't ignore Petra's anonymous tip. The hotel prepares for the Vale family's annual anniversary dinner, and every staff member becomes a suspect: the porter Dov, the chef, the night auditor. Emotional beat: suspicion corroding a workplace that functions like family.

chapters.title: A File Too Clean
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She discovers the official case file was accessed twice from an internal terminal — once by her own supervisor. Meanwhile Petra notices the confession letter quotes an error that exists only in the file, not in reality. The killer didn't witness the death; he studied its paperwork. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal, the law itself compromised.

chapters.title: Dov's Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Evidence mounts against Dov, the young porter Petra mentored — his key card, his temper, his debts. But the evidence is arranged too neatly, like a stage set. Petra realizes whoever framed Dov knows how Petra thinks, because Petra trained half the staff to notice things. Emotional beat: fear for someone he loves like a brother.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hidden in the late owner's effects, Petra and Ilsa find a ledger of hush payments dating back decades — survival money paid to keep staff silent about a fire that killed two workers years ago. The theme crystallizes: someone survived that fire by doing something unforgivable. Emotional beat: grief for the dead and fury at the living.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A second letter arrives, taunting: it predicts exactly what Petra will do next, and announces another death at the anniversary dinner unless he stops investigating. Petra understands the killer wants an audience — wants him specifically. He decides to give the killer a performance worth watching. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Murder
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, uneasy alliance. Petra proposes an illegal trap: feed the killer a false detail that exists nowhere in any file — a fabricated change to the dinner seating. Only the true murderer can react to it. Ilsa risks her career agreeing to work outside procedure. Emotional beat: trust built between two people who trust no institutions.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. At the dinner, the false detail is sprung; the night auditor, Silas — a fire survivor who killed Marguerite to bury the ledger — takes the bait and moves to silence the last witness. Petra confronts him publicly, using the killer's perfect knowledge of the file against him: Silas recites a fact that never happened. Emotional beat: high-wire tension breaking into catharsis.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Living
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, resolution. Silas confesses, and the ledger forces the city to reckon with the fire's true cost; Dov is cleared. Petra must decide whether to hand over his notes on the three earlier cases — justice outside the law versus the system's slow machinery. He gives them to Ilsa, keeping only the letters. The staff, his found family, raises a glass at a belated dinner. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, the price of survival finally named.
